title: Does the loop hold together?

data.source: Integrated information theory (Tononi 2004; Balduzzi and Tononi 2008; Oizumi, Albantakis and Tononi 2014). Two simplified measures computed exactly on an eight-state toy loop.

prediction: IIT would give a CRR-shaped toy loop a phi above zero only if the seed is both rewritten and read. A seed that is read by nothing, or never rewritten, gives zero. More carry-over gives less integration, not more. CRR itself says nothing about experience.
baseline: Integrated information theory (Tononi 2004; Oizumi, Albantakis and Tononi 2014): a feed-forward system has phi = 0. Decoy: a seed that is written and never read.
why: All five predictions about the toy held. R1 to R6 have no term for experience, so nothing of CRR's could be tested. Shared: both care whether what is carried forward is used. Left over: IIT says which systems are conscious; CRR is silent. It would become testable only if CRR stated what a cut or a seed has to do with experience.

forks.hand as two bits: noise shared between parts; cut ill-defined; not run

weighs: No outcome could count for or against CRR, which makes no claim here.
result: The full toy loop scored 0.27807 bits of toy phi (the weaker of two one-way cuts: 0.27807 and 0.29356). A seed that is written and never read scored 0.0. A seed that is never rewritten scored 0.0. As the carry-over q rose in four steps from none to nine tenths the score went 0.27807, 0.27807, 0.22626, 0.05141. As the coupling rose in four steps from weak to strong it went 0.02905, 0.11871, 0.27807, 0.29356. The older whole-minus-sum measure gave 0.50867 for the full loop and 0.248 for the seed that is never read, where toy phi gave zero.

precise_core: Phi is defined exactly within each version, but the definition has changed four times and critics have shown it is not unique.
proved_by_others: Independent groups compute, vary and criticise the measures (Barrett, Seth, Mediano, Oizumi, Aaronson).
differing_prediction: It differs clearly from workspace theories on where and how consciousness shows in the brain. Its sharpest claims need a phi that cannot be computed for a brain.
tested: A pre-registered adversarial collaboration with a rival theory (results reported from 2023). Phoenix calls it the one metaphysics-adjacent theory to have submitted to such a test.
passed: Mixed: some predictions held and some failed, for both theories. Phoenix records "mixed".
replicated: The perturbational complexity index, which IIT inspired, replicates across clinics. It is not phi.
engineering: The complexity index is used in research on patients who cannot respond. Phi itself is used for nothing.
admits_open_problems: It states that phi is intractable. Critics say its central claims are shielded from test; its authors dispute that.

precise_core: R1 to R6 are written exactly, with status keys. The parts are free choices: no universal q, ruler, dynamics or memory kernel (Phoenix: OPEN).
proved_by_others: Nobody outside the owner's programme. Phoenix says its own audit is not independent. Tonight's re-checks were made by model workers, not by independent people.
differing_prediction: Only through added bridges (the change clock, the regeneration law). Phoenix: the core has not yet issued a prediction.
tested: The bridges were frozen and scored on held-out real data inside the programme. No outside group has tested anything.
passed: Phoenix: no held-out CRR-specific pass; its result ledger is empty. Tonight's library ledger has no fits.
replicated: None. The one inherited first-level pass did not replicate (Phoenix).
literature: No peer-reviewed paper on CRR is cited anywhere in Phoenix, and none is known to this check.
engineering: Engineering candidates and good-practice rules only. Phoenix grades the method they rest on as known prior art.
admits_open_problems: An OPEN list in the core itself, failures kept on the ledger, and written exit conditions.

status.note: Scores are 0 to 3 on the stated scale. A line marked from_memory was not checked against a source tonight. The total is a count of ticks, not a ranking of truth.
